# Psalm 35 — Disagreement Log
**Generated by:** SOPHIA | **Threshold:** <70% word overlap

---

## 35:4 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** Let-them-be-put-to-shame and-dishonored, those-seeking my-soul; let-them-be-turned-back and-humiliated, those-devising my-harm.
- **LOGOS:** Let them be put to shame and dishonor who seek after my life! Let them be turned back and disappointed who devise evil against me!
- **PNEUMA:** Bring shame and disgrace on those trying to kill me; turn them back and humiliate those who plan to harm me.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

- **LOGOS:** Let their way be dark and slippery, with the angel of the LORD pursuing them!
- **PNEUMA:** Make their path dark and slippery, with the angel of the LORD pursuing them.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 35:8 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** Let-destruction come-upon-him unawares, and-his-net which he-hid catch-him; into-destruction let-him-fall.
- **LOGOS:** Let destruction come upon him when he does not know it! And let the net that he hid ensnare him; let him fall into it — to his destruction!
- **PNEUMA:** So let sudden ruin come upon them! Let them be caught in the trap they set for me! Let them be destroyed in the pit they dug for me.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

- **EMET:** And-my-soul shall-rejoice in-YHWH; it-shall-exult in-His-salvation.
- **LOGOS:** Then my soul will rejoice in the LORD, exulting in His salvation.
- **PNEUMA:** Then I will rejoice in the LORD. I will be glad because He rescues me.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 35:14 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** As-a-friend, as-a-brother to-me I-went-about; as-one-mourning a-mother, [in] gloom I-bowed-down.
- **LOGOS:** I went about as though I grieved for my friend or my brother; as one who laments his mother, I bowed down in mourning.
- **PNEUMA:** I was sad, as though they were my friends or family, as if I were grieving for my own mother.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

- **LOGOS:** like profane mockers at a feast, they gnash at me with their teeth.
